sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes and with a Finger.
Recognize details in shapes and objects as being similar or different from each other.
Tell a story using pictures.
Follow lines with a finger.

activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare illustrations
• Show pupils how to open their Pupil Books to the 
first page. Hold up the pupils Book so that pupils 
can see the page for lesson 1 and point to the 
first illustration.
• Say: Tegal sa baaraam ci nataal bu njékka bi mu mel nii. Ban Rab moo nekka nii? Waaw 
nag la.
• Point to the next picture in the row, to the right of the bull.
• Say: Nanu teg sunu baaraam ci nataal bu njékka bi. Ndax benna la ak bu ci toppa? 
Déedéet!"
• Point to the next picture in the row. 
• Say: Xoolleen ci bu ci toppa. Ndax niroo na ak bu njékka bi? Déedéet!"
• Point to the final picture in the row. 
• Say: "Ndax bii niroo na ak bu njékka bi? Waaw!"
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the first   
illustration and find the other illustration in the row that matches. 

Compare shapes
• Ask pupils to turn to the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Use the same process as the activity above with the shapes on the next page of the Pupil 
Book.

activities.title: Story sequence
activities.content:
Tell a story using pictures
• Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Say: "Tegleen seen baaraam ci nataal bu njékka bi. Lan la nit ki di def?"
• Call on two pupils to respond.
• Talk with pupils about each picture in the sequence (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Ask pupils what   
 the people are doing in each picture and ask questions to help them think about the   
 pictures.
• Ask pupils to look at the pictures and describe the story the pictures are telling. Help   
 them see that the woman is preparing "banku".

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger 
· Show the next page in the Pupil Book. 
· Say: "Lan la xale bu góor bi ci nataal bi di def? Accaleen nu jàppale ko mu wexa kupe   
 bi ci mbaal gi! Ndax pare ngeen? jëfooleen seen baaraam yi ngir ngeen wone fi kupe   
 bi war a jaar." 
· Show pupils how to trace the line from the ball to the goal with a finger. 
· Say: "Lan la golo gi di def? Lan ngeen foog ne moom la bëgga?" 
· Watch as pupils trace the line from the monkey to the banana with a finger.  
· Repeat with the remaining image.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Recognize the front cover, and title of a book.
Apply new words learned to own life and use new words in conversation.
Use background knowledge to build meaning.
Use verbal and nonverbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: Parts of a Book
activities.content:
Recognize the Grade parts of a book - cover, 
back, Title
• Point to the cover and back of a book.
• Say: Danoo jànge ci kanam jém ci ganaaw. 
• Say: Baat yi ci kanam xët mi moo noo wax boppi 
téere bi. Boppi téere bi moo noo wax lan la noo 
jànga.
• Say: "Sunu àggee ca ngeexteelu léeb bi, dina nu gis ganaaw téere bi."

activities.title: Vocabulary – before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask pupils 
what they know about each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If 
needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know. 
  ngédda, naqar, nafar

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud
• Use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available
While reading, pause to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key moments such as when you 

come to a vocabulary word the pupils just learned. 

     Faatu dafa tuuti 
Faatu dafa am naqar, mu ngi toog ci kër gi deful dara, mu gis bàjjenam mu ngee wol ngir tay 
cere, mu ne ko, "bàjjen ndax mën naa laa dimbale"? Mu  ne ko "déedéet Faatu li ngaa jéem 
dafa bari lool." Mu jóge fa dem yoonam.
Faatu gis kalam bi mu ngee lem yéréem yi. Mu ne ko, "Ndax mën naa laa dimbale?" Mu ne ko, 
"Déedéet Faatu li ngaa jéem dafa bari lool." Mu jóge fa dem yoonam
Faatu gis magam bu góor mu ngee witta ci ngéddam li, mu ne ko, "Ndax mën naa laa 
dimbale?" Mu ne ko, "Déedéet Faatu, li ngaa jéem dafa bari lool." Mu jóge fa dem yoonam. 
Faatu gis magam bu jigéen mu ngee nafar li mu jàngoon ci daara ji, mu ne ko "Ndax mën naa 
laa dimbale?" Mu ne ko "Déedeet Faatu, li ngaa jéem dafa bari lool." Mu jóge fa dem yoonam.
Mujanteel ba mu daje ak baayam. Baayam ne ko, "Faatu suma xarit bi lan moo tax nga mer? 
Sawaruloo dara."
Faatu ne ko, "Xanaa dama mën lu bari su fekkee ne damaa  wol ngir tay cere, xanaa damaa  
mën lu bari su fekkee ne damaa  lem yéré. Xanaa damaa mën lu bari su fekkee ne damaa  
witta ci ngédda. Xanaa damaa  mën lu bari su fekkee ne damaa  nafar njànga. Léegi, lan laa 
war a def?"
Baayam ne ko, "Faatu bu la dara naqari suma doom! Màggal rek be raw, man soxla naa ku 
mën lu bari be mën maa dimbale ma def suma soraas yi ci leket. Ndax di nga ma dimbale?" 
Faatu dimbale baayam, mu bég.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review the parts of a book - cover, back, title
• Call on a volunteer pupil to show the class which part of a book you start reading from. 
Ask what this part of the book it is called. (correct response: ("front page")
• Say: Fan la boppi léeb bi nekka? (:Tontu: Ci kow léeb bi")
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer. Call on a second volunteer pupil to say the title of the 
story that was just read aloud.
• Say: Lan la noo gis sunu àggee ci njeextelu téere bi? " Tontu: Feggu mu ci ganaaw''
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer and point to the back of the book.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes, and with a finger.
Recognize details in letter shapes as being similar or different from each other
Follow lines with their finger.

activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare shapes of capital letters 
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see 
the page and point to the first capital letter. 
Do not say the name of the letter - this is 
NOT an activity for pupils to learn letters. It 
is an activity for pupils to practice telling the 
difference between letter and shapes.
• Say:  Dégluleen te xool fii, maa ngee joxoñ ci araf bu njékka bi
• Say: Bu kenna joxoñ. Danoo seet bu niroo ak bi ma joxoñ."
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: Accaleen nu teg sunu baaraam ci araf bu njékka bi. Ndax niroo na ak bu ma 
joxoñoon? Déedéet!
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: Xoolleen ci bi ci toppa. Ndax niroo na ak bu njékka bi? Déedéet!"
• Point to the final one in the row.
• Say: "Accaleen nu xool bu ci toppa. Ndax niroo na ak bu ma joxoñoon? 
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the first 
capital letter and find the other one in the row that matches it. 

Compare shapes
• Use the same process as the activity above with the small letters on the next page of the  
 Pupil Book. Do not say the name of the letter - this is NOT an activity for pupils to learn   
 letters. It is an activity for pupils to practice telling the difference between letter shapes.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see the four objects in the next activity. Ask 
pupils to point to the objects in their own books.
• Call on pupils to describe what images go together and why (there is no 1 correct answer).

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger
· Say: Accaleen nu toppa rab yu sew yii! Bu njékka bi saleer la! Accaleen nu teg sunu 
baaraam te toppa fi mu war a tób di jaar ci kow xët mi.
· Demonstrate following the line on the page as needed.
· Repeat with the remaining images.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Know that words are separated by spaces.
Use new words correctly in sentences.
Answer factual questions.
Use verbal and non-verbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: Words are separated by spaces
activities.content:
Describe what a word is, and why there are 
spaces between them
• Take out the read aloud book from yesterday's 
lesson.Choose a sentence to write on the board.
• Say: Kàddu bii mu ngi jóge ci léeb bu ma leen léebaloon. Di nanu waxtaane diggante yu nu 
fekka ci baat yi ci kàddu gi. Su maa jànga, damaa  jànga baat yi benna benna, ndax baat 
bu nekka dafa am lu mu tekki.
• Point to a word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
• Point to the space after the word.

• Say: "Diggante yi ci baat yi ñoo maa won nu baat yi taxawee ak tàmblee beneen bu ci 
toppa."
• Point to the following word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
• Say: "Diggante yu ci baat yi ñoo leen a dimbale ngeen mën a jànga. Sooleen di binda ay 
kàddu, dangeen di tàqale baat yi."
• Write another sentence. Choose a volunteer to help demonstrate on the new sentence.
• Say: Tegal sa baaraam ci ron baat bi. Léegi, won ma baat bu ci toppa. Naka ngeen a wonee 
ne tàqale nanu ñaari baat yii? (Tontu: Baat yi am nanu ay diggante).
• Pick up the book. Walk around the room. Ask 3 pupils to find a space between two   
 words, and put their fingers on it.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes and with a finger.
Recognize sight words.
Read sentences using sight words and pictures.
Draw simple shapes.

activities.title: Read sight words
activities.content:
Learn two new sight words
• Point to the pictures of the boy and girl in the 
Pupil Book.
• Say: Kii moo di Móodu. Kii moo di Faatu. Di nanu 
jànga lu bari ci ñoom ci xaaj bii ci at mi. 
• Say: Tegleen seen baaraam ci ron nataalu xale bu góor bi Móodu. Tegleen seen baaraam  
  ci ron nataalu xale bu jigéen bi Faatu.
· Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (matching activity).
• Ask pupils to point to Móodu on the left side, then point to the matching name on the   
 right side. Repeat with Faatu.
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (box with boy and girl names).
• Ask pupils to say the first name in the left column, then point to the matching name in the  
 row.
· Continue in the same way with each row.

activities.title: Read a sentence
activities.content:
Read a sentence using sight words
• Say:  "Gis naa [FAATU] ci kow xët mi. Léegi gis na baat bu bees! Baat bu bees bii moo 
di [gis]. Ndégam xam nanu [FAATU] ak baat bu bees bi, mën nanoo jànga lu nataal yi di 
wax."
• Point to the first picture sentence on the page in the Pupil Book. Ask pupils to name the 
picture on the right.
• Read the picture sentence aloud to pupils, showing them how you point to the pictures/
word with your finger as you read.
• Continue to the next picture sentence. Ask pupils to point to the boy.

• Point to pictures or words as you read. ( Móodu gis na béy]) 
• Remind pupils that " gis na" means "to observe" or "to see." 
• Make a gesture to demonstrate seeing. Then, ask pupils to read the picture sentence 
again together.
• Say: "Léegi, kan ngeen gis ci ron nataal bi? Accaleen nu teg sunu baaraam ci kàddu gi te 
jàngandoor ko [FAATU gis na taabul]  
• Say: Kan moo mën a jànga kàddu gu ci toppa?"
• Continue calling on pupils to read the picture sentences until the end of the page.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects 
· Point to the next activity in the Pupil Book.
• Say:  Nanu teg sunu baaraam ci ron nataal bu njékka bi. Lan ngeen gis? Ndax gis ngeen 
toogu bu ci toppa?
• Point to the next picture in the row. 
• Say: " Waaw, nag wi! Lan moo uutale nag wi ak xar mi?"
• Continue with other illustrations.

activities.title: Draw shapes
activities.content:
Practice drawing common shapes
·  Ask pupils to trace each shape in the Pupil Book with one finger.
· Ask pupils to try to draw 3 of each shape in their exercise books. Depending on their   
 comfort with writing and drawing, different pupils may focus on just one shape or draw   
 many.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes and with a finger
Use new words correctly in sentences.
Use verbal and non-verbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: How to read – track with a finger
activities.content:
Teach how to track words with a finger
• Say: "Am na ay  yoon yu nu war a toppa sunu dee 
wax walla déglu ay baat ak ay kàddu yu nu war 
a toppa.  Yoon yi dina nu jàppale ngir nu xam lu 
noo wax ci nun. Tey nanu déglu kàddu bu bees"
• Write a sentence on the board. Demonstrate how to track with your finger under each 
word as you read. Be sure to place and pause your finger under the specific word.
• Call on a pupil at random to describe what to do with a finger while reading.
• Call on 2 pupils to demonstrate tracking words of the sentence on the board while you 
read it aloud.

activities.title: Vocabulary – Before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask pupils 
what they know about each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If 
needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know. 
jéem, naqar, bég

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Reread the following story aloud
• use the appropriate big book or  supplementary illustrations if available
• Partway through the story, pause to show pupils how you track reading with your finger 

below each word you read as you read it. At the end of the line of text, make a big 
sweeping motion back to the start of the next line of text. Continue tracking with your 
finger.
• After demonstrating, complete the read aloud. 

      Aadama dafa Sibiru 

Aadama dafa dékka ak wayjuram yi, yaayam ak baayam mu ngi toog, néeg bi wéet ne tekk,nu 
oote ne "Aadama, Aadama" tontuwuleen. Ana Aadama? Aadama dégga na leen waay uyuwul 
mu ngi tédda rek ci lal bi
Wayjuram yi xoolante, yaayam daw dugga ci néegi Aadama ne ko: "Aadama jàmma nga 
fanaan?" "Naka nga def?" Aadama ne ko: "Yaay dama feebar"
Yaayam tek loxom ci jéyam  bi ne ko danga am tàngat, xaaral ma oo fajkat bi, baayam oo 
fajkat bi ci telefun, fajkat bi  ñów seet Aadama be sottal ne ko danga sibiru. Dinaa la jox 
garabi sibiru. Biiri Aadama bi di métti, mu laaj fajkat bi ne ko: "Ndax damaa  dee?" Fajkat bi 
ree ne ko "Déedéet Aadama Dinaa la jox garab yu baax be nga wér te di nga nelaw." Yaayam 
gérém fajkat bi ne ko jéréjéf. Fajkat bi wax wayjuri Aadama ne leen: bu leen fàtte di ko jox 
garabam yi te joxee ko ni ma leen ko waxee waay na di tédda ci sanke bu am garab ngir aaru 
ci sibiru. Yaayam xool baayam ne ko: nanu jendi sanke bu am garab tey. Baayam daw dem 
gaaw ca jaba ja jéndi sanke bu am garab.
Aadama tédda ci lal bi di déglu seen waxtaan wi.
Lii dafa mel ni léebu xale waay dafa noo jàngal ni noo fagaroo ci sibiru, tédda ci sanke bu 
am garab ni mu ame njériñ ci fegu ci yoo yi ak boo ame sibiru nga dem faju ji ci fajkat yi ci 
lopitaan/ fajuwaay yi.

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning in their 
own words.
• Say: Léegi nanu jél baat yi nu jànga nu tabax ay kàddu.
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in the pupil 
book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word in 
a new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct 
the pupils, depending on the responses.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review tracking words with a finger
• Ask a volunteer pupil to tell you something you should do to be sure you don't skip words 
while reading. (Correct response - track the words with your finger, or follow under the 
words with your finger, etc.)
• Ask one pupil to demonstrate tracking for the class using the book.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Review the question word "Who" ("kan")
• Read the question: 
• Say: Kan moo oo fajjkat bi ba Aadama feebare?: (Baayi Aadama moo ko ooyoon doktoor ba 
Aadama feebare. 
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "Kan" is asking about. Call on 
one or two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why. 
(Response: the question word "Kan" asks us the name of a someone or something alive)
• Teach pupils to use the question word "Fan"
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, "Fan" Tell pupils that they will  
 use it to answer the next question. 

· Read the question: 
• Say: Soo feebare fan nga war a dem?
• Say: Baatu "fan" moo noo wax tontul béréb tolluwaay. Su ma déggee "Fan" Dinaa xam ne   
   tontu bi béréb la. 
· Read the question: 
• Say: "Fan la Aadama nekkoon bi ko yaayam ak baayam di oo?" Answer: ("Aadama mu ngi 

woon ci néegam bi ko yaayam ak baayam di oo)"
• Say: Fan lanu jàngoon ci léeb bi di wax ne: ba léegi mu ngaitédda ca lal ba.
• Ask pupils to think about "where", or the place, that this happened.
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: Fan la baayi Aadama jéndee sanke?  Baayi Aadama mu ngi jénde 
sanke ca jaba ja.
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to taldindi¿ k about their answers 
to the question. Remind pupils that it is a "where"question.
• Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Evaluate pupils use of the keyword "where" ("Fan")
• Say: Ban baat ci léeb bi moo noo wax mbiri béréb ci léeb bi?
• Call on a pupil at random who raised their hand. Remind them that the word is "where" 
(Fan )

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Display mastery of key skills learned over the last four lessons: the parts of a book, spaces between words and tracking a finger under print.

activities.title: Assessment
activities.content:
Special assessment - assess week 1 skills:
• Know what the "cover " and "back " of the 
book means.
• Understand that words in print are separated 
by spaces. 
• Know that tracking a finger under a word helps 
keep track of where you are reading.

1. Know what the "cover" and "back" of the book means.
• Hand out pupil books
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "front". Give feedback and explain. Give 
more examples if needed. If you see any pupil struggling, make sure to support them in 
this skill during the next lessons.
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "back" of the book. Give feedback, and   
 explain and give more examples if needed. 

2. Understand that words in print are separated by spaces
• Ask pupils to turn to the first decodable story in their book. Show them the picture for the 
story, so they can find the story in the book. They will not be able to read this story yet, 
but that is alright. Do not ask them to read the story.
• Point to the "space" between the first two words in the story. Ask all pupils to put their 
finger on that space. Walk around and show them where to put their finger.
• Ask pupils to point to the next space in the story. Walk around to observe and give 
feedback.
• Ask pupils to raise their hand if they know what that space is for (why it's there). 
• Ask a volunteer to answer. Ask another pupil if the response is correct.
• Say: Diggante yi ci baat yi moo laa wax ne baat yi dañu uute. 

3. Know that tracking a finger under a word helps keep track of where you are reading
• Open a big book (any big book) to the first page. Ask pupils to watch and listen. Read the 
first sentence while pointing to (tracking) each word with your finger.
• Ask pupils what you were doing with your finger. Then ask them why you did that. Tell the 
pupil who responds if they are correct or not. Then repeat or say the correct response. 
(Possible response: I was tracking a finger under the words as I read them. Tracking with 
a finger helps you know where you are while reading, so you don't get confused or lost.)

activities.content:

• Look at the list of key skills below. Choose one that your pupils need to practice. Ask

Key activities from week 1 lessons

 2. Read sentences with sight words 
 3. Choose the letter that matches the first letter in the row 
 4. Recognize sight words (character names)

Recognize sight words, and read them in a sentence.

activities.title: Story sequence
activities.content:
Tell a story using pictures
• Point to the picture story in the Pupil Book. 
• Say: Tegal sa baaraam ci nataal bu njékka bi. Lan 
la nit ki di def?
• Call on two pupils to respond.

• Talk with pupils about each picture in the sequence (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Ask pupils what the 
people are doing in each picture and ask questions to help them think about the pictures.
• Ask pupils to look at the pictures and describe the story the pictures are telling.

activities.title: Read a sentence using sight words
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to independently read the picture sentences using the sight words they learned 
yesterday. Walk around the room to monitor and help pupils as needed. Ensure that pupils 
are reading from left to right and tracking the pictures/words with their finger.
• After giving pupils an opportunity to read the sentences, call on pupils at random to read 
aloud the first 6 picture sentences.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the Letter
• Point to the lowercase letter /a/ on the alphabet 
poster or on the board.
• Say: Bii moo di sunu arafu tey bi. Riiru araf bii 
moo di /a/. Accaleen nu waxandoor: /a/
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the uppercase letter "A" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Bii benna araf bi la rek. Moom itam riiru /a/ la. Nii lanu koo gise su dee tàmbali kàddu 
walla tur. 
• Point to the lower case letter "a" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Li ci gën a bari, nii lanu ko dee binde ci baat yi.
• Say: A rafnga la, rafnga lu am solo la ci baat bi ndax saa yoo di tabax baat foog mu am   
 rafnga.

activities.title: Teach pupils to hear syllables
activities.content:
Clap two-syllable words
• Say: Baat bu nekka mën nanu koo dog ay dogiti baat. Dogiti baat bu ne am ab riiri rafnga. 
Melni nu nu ko jàngewoon /a/, /nda/ (papa).
• Model by clapping:  →  pa/pa
• Practice together with pupils:  Papa →  pa/pa, bale →  ba/le
• Pupils practice alone: almet →  al/met, baka → /ba  ka /
• Clap words with different numbers of syllables

• Say: Baat yii am nanu ñaari dogiti baat, waay baat bi mën naa am benna dogiti baat, ñaari 
dogiti baat, ñetti dogiti baat, walla lu ko óppa. Accaleen nu jéem ay baat seet. Dinaa wax 
baat bi njékka. Léegi, nanu ko tàccundoor- ñaari yoon. 
 Words: faloo:  mata: ma/ta, dimbale: dim/ba/le, taxale: ta/xa/le

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: Lan ngeen gis?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help   
 pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: Accaleen nu tàccu dogiti baat yi ci baatu"(papa) Ñaata yoon ngeen dégga riiri /a/     
 ci baatu (papa)? Accaleen nu tàccuwaat.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the  
 sound, help them by saying another word with that sound in your Wolof or another   
 Wolof they know.
• Say: Accaleen nu waxandoor baat bu ci toppa - (yaay). Ndax dégga ngeen rafnga   
 /a/ ci baatu (yaay)? Ñaata yoon ngeen ko dégga?
• Say:Léegi nag yeen la. Waxleen baat bi. Tegleen seen baaraam ci ron arafu 'a' su   
 ngeen koo wax, di ngeen def riiru /a/. 

Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Na ku nekka teg baaraamam ci ron nataal bu nu marke "yaay"
• Say: Lan ngeen gis? "yaay" la.
• Clap the syllables with the pupils. 
• Say: Mën na noo xécca riiru /a/. Bu noo wax riir bi da nu koo xécca. Ndax dégga nanu    
 riiru rafnga "aa" ci baatu "yaay"?  
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the   
 same vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to  
 each other. Answer: two
• Tell pupils that when they see two /a/ together, it makes a long sound /aa/. The long   
 sound means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to  
 repeat. 
• Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long    
 (stretched) sound.

• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the   
 syllables and listen for the long vowel in the word

activities.title: Writing – Letter
activities.content:
Write the letter and say its sound

• Air write the letter (use a straight arm), and say its sound as you write. Pupils should   
then try it two more times while you watch and provide feedback.
• Demonstrate writing the letter on the chalkboard once more.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter 5 times.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:

 illustrations if available)

     Ismayla Ak Liggéeykatam Yi
Dafa amoon benna baykat bu tudda Ismayla, dafa amoon tool wu yaatu, benna bés mu soxla 
nu ko dimbale ci liggéeyi tool bi.
Mu dem ci max ne ko: "Max dama bëgga nga ñów dimbale ma liggéey ci suma tool bi élég." 
Max ne ko: "Su fekkee ne ganaar du  ñów, ak ay cuujam Dinaa  ñów ." Ismayla ne ko: 
"Déedéet! Ganaar du ñów." Mu dem ci ganaar ne ko: "Ganaar dama bëgga nga  ñów dimbale 
ma liggéey ci suma tool wi élég." Ganaar ne ko: "Su fekkee ne céeli du  ñów, Dinaa  ñów." 
Ismayla ne ko: "Déedéet! Céeli du  ñów." Mu dem ci céeli ne ko: "Dama bëgga nga  ñów 
dimbale ma ci suma tool bi élég." Céeli ne ko: "Su fekkee ne róbbakat du  ñów, Dinaa  ñów." 
Ismayla ne ko: "Déedéet! Róbbakat du  ñów." Mu dem ci r óbbakat ne ko: "Dama bëgga nga  
ñów dimbale ma ci suma tool bi élég. Róbbakat ne ko: "Su fekkee ne jaan du  ñów, Dinaa  
ñów." Ismayla ne ko: "Déedéet! Jaan du  ñów." Mu dem ci jaan ne ko: "Dama bëgga nga  ñów 
dimbale ma liggéey ci suma tool bi élég." Jaan ne ko: "Su fekkee ne et du  ñów, Dinaa  ñów." 
Ismayla ne ko "Déedeet! et du  ñów." Mu dem ci et ne ko: "Dama bëgga nga  ñów dimbale 
ma ci suma tool bi élég." Et ne ko: "Su fekkee ne safara du  ñów, Dinaa  ñów." Ismayla ne ko: 
"Déedéet! Safara du  ñów." Ismayla dem ci safara ne ko: "Dama bëgga nga  ñów dimbale ma 
ci suma tool bi élég." Safara ne ko: "Su fekkee ne taw du  ñów, Dinaa  ñów."
 Ca élég sa ci suba, liggéeykat yu Ismayla santoon liggéey ba yép ñów. Ganaar ga lekka Max.
Céeli ba daqee Ganaar ak cuujam ya. Róbbakat ba rey Céeli.
Jaan ja màtta Róbbakat ba.  
Et ba dòor Jaan ja. 

Safara lakka et ba. Taw ba fey safara sa. 
Ismayla daw dem.

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
· Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
· Call on 3 pupils at random to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the   
 meaning in their own words. Ask pupils how the word was used in the story.
· Say: Accaleen nu jél baat yu fés yi nu jàngoon te tabax ay kàddu.
· Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in the pupil  
 book or read aloud.
· For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word   
 in  a new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help,   
 or correct the pupils, depending on the responses.

activities.title: Sight word review

Review the sight words from last week

di gis ci su nu ngànga. Ndax fàtteleku ngeen turi xale bu jigéen bi ak turi xale bu góor bi?

point to the correct name when you call it out. If so, congratulate them. If not, help them by 
having them point at each one, and repeat the correct name with you. Then try again with the 
same student to be sure he or she knows the word.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
· Review the question word "where" ("Fan")
· Read the question:  
·  Say: "Ndax fàtteleku ngeen baat bunu jëfoowoon di laajte li nu jànga ci.
·  Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
·  Say: "Ndax fàtteleku ngeen baat bu nu jëfoo woon di laajte lu nu jànga  ci fan yii    
 weesu?" Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "where" is asking    
 about. Call on one or two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or   

 incorrect and why. (Response: the question word "where" asks us about a place) 

Teach pupils to use the question word "when" ("kañ")
·  Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, "when". Tell pupils that they 
will use it to answer the next question.
·  Read the question: Kañ nga dee bëgga di fo ci biti?
·  Call on 2 pupils to answer. Their answer should be a time (i.e. in the morning, after   
school, on the weekend)
·  Say: Baatu "kañ" (Baati laajte waxtu la) danu koo jëfandikoo ci laajte waxtu. Suma 
déggee "kañ," Dinaa xam ne tontu bi waxtu la di doon. Mën na nekka waxtu ci  bés bi (mel 
ni ci suba),  bés ci  bés bu ay bi (mel ni Àjjuma) walla diir ci at mi. (mel ni nawet).

·  Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers to the  
 question. 
·  Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "i" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Bii moo di sunu arafu tey bi. Riiru araf bii moo di /i/. Accaleen nu waxandoor: /i/
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the capital letter "I" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: see it like this. 
Lii benna araf bi la rek. Moom itam riiru /i/ la. Su dee tàmbali kàddu walla tur, nii  lanu 
koo gise.
• Point to the small letter "i" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Di nanu koo gise nii ci ay baat ci lu bari.

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: Lan ngeen gis?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help 
pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: Accaleen nu tàccu dogiti baat yi ci baati  (diw). Ñaata yoon ngeen dégga riiru /i/ ci 
baat tu "diw"? Accaleen nu tàccuwaat.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the 
sound, help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or in another 
language they know.
• Say: Accaleen nu waxandoor baat bi ci toppa. Baat bi ci toppa moo di "nit". Ndax dégga 
ngeen riiru /i/ ci baati "nit"? Ñaata yoon ngeen ko dégga?
• Say: Léegi nag yéen la. Waxleen baat bi. Tegleen seen baaraam ci ron arafi /i/ te wax riir 
bi.
Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Na ku nekka teg baaraamam ci ron nataal bu njékka bi ci suuf. Lan ngee gis? Lii moo 
di " xiir" 
Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: Riiru /i/ mën naa xéccu. Li moo firndél  moo di Danoo xécca riir bi mu gudda. Ndax 
dégga ngeen rafnga bu gudda /ii/ ci baat tu "xiir"?
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the 
same vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to 
each other. (Answer: two)
• Tell pupils that when they see two "i" together, it makes a long sound /ii/. The long sound 
means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to 
repeat. 
• Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long 
(stretched) sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the 
syllables and listen for the long vowel in the word.

During reading, stop to discuss people, place, and time

where they think the story takes place. What time do they think it is? What do they think 
the character(s) is/are like? Assure pupil responses are related to the picture.

Kumba ak wayjuram yi ñoo dékkoon. Ñu ngi am ci kër gi ñaari mbaam xuux, ñetti ganaar,

nekka ci liggéeyam. Mu daw dem ci magam bu jigéen bi ne ko: Awa, kaay seet lu bon lu béy 
di def?" Magam bu jigèen bi ne ko: "kumba bàyyil nettali." nekka ci liggéeyam. Mu daw 
dem ci maamam ne ko: "Maam, kaay seet lu bon li béy def." Maamam nekkuloon di def 
dara, mu ne ko: "Kumba nanu dem nga won ma ko." Ñu ànda daw dem ca béy ba, fekka ko

yi." Yaayam daw ñow yuuxu ne: "Ana suma carax yi?" Baayam daw ñów yuuxu ne: "Ana 
suma tubéy ji?" Magam bu góor daw ñów yuuxu ne: "Ana suma mbàjja gi?" Magam bu 
jigéen bi daw ñów yuuxu ne: "Ana suma (yunifom) bi?" Ñoom ñép xool béy, béy xoolleen,

nekka ci liggéeyam. Mu daw dem ci maamam ne ko: "Maam, kaay seet lu bon li béy def." Maamam 
nekkuloon di def dara, mu ne ko: "Kumba nanu dem nga won ma ko." Ñu ànda daw dem ca béy ba, 
fekka ko mu ngee yéy yéréem ya. Maam yuuxu, "Laay layla laaaa! Béy baa ngee lekka suma yéré 
yi." Yaayam daw ñow yuuxu ne: "Ana suma carax yi?" Baayam daw ñów yuuxu ne: "Ana suma 
tubéy ji?" Magam bu góor daw ñów yuuxu ne: "Ana suma mbàjja gi?" Magam bu jigéen bi daw ñów 
yuuxu ne: "Ana suma (yunifom) bi?" Ñoom ñép xool béy, béy xoolleen, meem di wàncal geenam gi. 
Maamam for yéréem yi, lénga Kumba ne ko: "Jëréjëf ci li nga daw ñów nettali ma li béy doon def.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Review the question word "Where" ("Fan")
· Read the first question: Fan la béy wi doon bajantoo? Answer: (béy baa ngi doon   
  bajantoo ci kër gi)
·  Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
· Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "where" is asking about. Call   
 on one or two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why.  
 (Response: the question word "where" asks us about a place)
Teach pupils to use the question word "what" ("Lan")
· Read the question: "Ban meññeef ngeen gën a bëgga?"
·  Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer.
·  Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, "what." Tell pupils that they   
 will use it to answer the next question.
·  Say: Baatu "Lan"dafa  noo wax nu jëfandoo dar a walla xelal ci tontu. Su ma déggee   
 "Lan", Dinaa xam ne tontu bi loo xam ne mën nga koo gis te laal ko, walla mbir mu jub.
·  Say: Su ma gisee rab bu bees ma laaj leen "lii lan la?" Dama bëgga xam turi rab bi. Su ma  
  laajtee, " lan" ? Bëgga naa xam  lan la mbiri ómba.
·  Read the question: Lan la yaa yi Kuumba di def? Answer: yaa yi kuumba ngi doon wal   
 fufu?
·  Say: Accaleen nu xelaat li nu jàngoon. Léeb bi mu ne: "Yaayam mu ngi doon liggéey walla  
  mu ngi doon wol dugub ngir tay cere."
·  Ask pupils to think about what, or the thing, they are asking about. 
·  Call on pupils at random to respond.
·  Read the question: Lan la Béy wi yéy? Tontu: (Béy bi yére la yéyóon)
·  Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers to   
 the question. Remind pupils that it is a "what" question.
·  Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

activities.title: Letter review
activities.content:
Review small and capital letters
• Write the small letter "i" and capital letter "I" 
on the blackboard. 
• Ask pupils to raise their hands if they know the 
sound the letter makes. Call on a pupil to say it.
• Provide feedback.
• Ask pupils to find and point to the letter in their 
book. Ask the whole class to say the sound.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "o" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
·  Say:  "This is our new letter for today. This letter makes the sound /O/. Say it with me: 
/i/." Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
·  Point: "Bii benna araf bi la rek. Moom itam riiru /o/ la. Su dee tàmbali kàddu walla tur, 
nii lanu koo gise."
·  Point to the capital letter "O" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
·  Say: Lii benna araf bi la rek. Moom itam riiru /O/ la. Su dee tàmbali kàddu walla tur, nii 
lanu koo gise.
·  Point to the small letter "o" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
·  Say: "Most times, we will see it like this in words."

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
Say: Lan ngeen gis?
Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help 
pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say:  Accaleen nu tàccu dogiti baat yi /go/lo/. Ñaata yoon ngeen dégga riiru /o/ ci baat bi 
"Golo"? Accaleen nu tàccuwaat dogiti baat yi.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the 
sound, help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or in another 
language they know.
• Say: Accaleen nu waxandoor baat bu ci toppa. 'Loxo' Dégga ngeen riiru /o/ ci baatu 'Loxo 
'? Ñaata yoon ngeen ko dégga?
Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Na ku nekka teg baaraamam ci ron nataal bi ñu marke "bool" ca suufam.
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: Riiru /o/ mën naa xéccu.  Li mu firi moo di Danoo xécca riir bi ba mu gudda. Ndax 
dégga ngeen rafnga bu gudda bii /oo/ ci baatu "bool"?
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the 
same vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to 
each other. Answer: two
• Tell pupils that when they see two "o" together, it makes a long sound /oo/. The long 
sound means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to 
repeat. 
• Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long 
(stretched) sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the   
 syllables and listen for the long vowel in the word.

lesson

pupils to follow along, tracking with their finger.

activities.title: How to read – using illustrations
activities.content:
Teach how to think about illustrations while reading
• Say:  Su noo xool nataal yi, dinanu jàngal nu xam lu bari ci léeb bi, ak lu mu ómba, fan la 
xewe ak kañ la xew. Tey Dinaa jànga léeb bi. Su maa jànga, dina nu taxaw te waxtaane 
nataal yu uute yi.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If 
needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know. 

Liggéey            Yérém              jëréjëf

activities.title: Read aloud (Big Boo)
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud 
·  see the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available)
·  During reading, stop to discuss people and things in the story.

·  Pause at 2-3 pictures throughout the book while reading. Ask pupils, based on the   
 picture, who they think the character(s) is/are. Also ask questions that use the word   
 "what." Assure pupil responses are related to the picture.
·  Possible questions (use these, or ask your own questions):
·  Who is going to the _____?
·  What is this thing? What kind of thing (for example, animal, house, etc.) is this? 
·  Talk a bit about how the picture relates to parts of the story you are reading aloud.

Baayam ne ko; "Aadama, kaay lekka! Ñam wu nga bëgga la." Waay Aadama xiiful.
Baayam gàcca ko, Waay Aadama xiiful.
Yaayam defal ko lekka ci palaatam bi, waay betey xiiful. Baayam lelli benna màngoro, fox jox ko ci 
ab foxit. Waay Aadama xiiful.
Yaayam ne ko; "Léegi nag sa waxtu lekka jot na." Aadama ne ko: "Yaay bóoy danga fàtte ne jox 
nga ma añ."

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
·  Ask pupils if they heard the new words during the read aloud.
·  Call on 3-4 pupils at random to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the   
 meaning in their own words.
·  Say: Accaleen nu jëfoo sunu baat yu fés yi ngir tabax ay kàddu.
·  Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in the   
 pupil book or read aloud.
·  For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word   
 in  a new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or   
 correct the pupils, depending on the responses

"E"

activities.title: Teach pupils to hear syllables
activities.content:
Clap words with different numbers of syllables
• Model by clapping syllables. Read the word once, then clap the syllables:  
dogiti: do/gi /ti,  
• Practice together with pupils. Read the word once, then clap the syllables with pupils.  
Yolomal : yo/lo/mal.
• Pupils practice alone. Read the word once, then ask pupils to clap the syllables 
independently (without the teacher). Xoolal keppa
• Give pupils feedback words they have difficulty with. Help them hear the syllable breaks.

activities.title: Pre-activity vocabulary
activities.content:
Discuss pictures
• Have pupils point to the first picture in the Pupil Book, "feer." Ask them what they think it 
is. Ask them what they know about it, or their experiences. (For example, "Have you seen 
this/it before?" "Where?" "What is it like?").
• Discuss each picture for 1 minute or less until the end of the page.

Pictures:
• Feer
• xorom
• bale
• bool
• xaal
 • xar 

Hear and see the vowel within a word
• Say: Joxoñleen nataal bu ñjékka bi. Lan la? (Confirm that what they say matches the word 
in the book, or correct it).
• Ask pupils to clap the syllables in the word once.
• Say: Accaleen nu xool dogiti baat yi te tàccu. Rafnga bi moo di /o/. Léegi tegleen seen 
baaraam ci ron riiru /oo/ bu ngeen jàngoon.
• Demonstrate in a pupil book by touching the first picture and the vowels that match the 
picture. Walk around the room so pupils can see your fingers on the correct picture and 
vowels.
• Ask pupils to repeat with the next picture. Clap the word with them. Then ask the pupils 
what vowel sounds they heard. Repeat, or say, the correct answer for the whole class to 
hear. Then ask the class to touch the picture and the vowels.
• Once pupils are comfortable with this, clap each word with them. After each word, ask 
them to find the matching vowels by themselves. 
• Check their work as they go.

activities.title: Sight word review
activities.content:
Review the sight words through shared writing
• Say: Léegi nanu jàngaat ñaari tur yu ci téere bi.
· Write the two sight words (MÓODU, FAATU) on the top of the board.
· Ask pupils to think of a place that these characters might like to go.
• Call on 3-4 pupils at random to give you some ideas. Guide pupils to choose a character 
name, and say where they might like to go. Write the sentences on the board. For 
example, FAATU dafa dee bëgga dem ca géej ga di  nappa jën. "Try to get at least 2 
examples for each character.
· Read the sentences back to pupils.

activities.content:
Review the question word "what" (" lan ")
· Read the question: Lan ngeen dee bëgga di def su ngeen wàcce iskul?
· Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer.
· Say: Jànga nanu ne baatu "Lan" moo noo wax nu jëfoo turi dara ngir tontu ab laaj.
· Say: Beneen mbir mu "Lan" mën a laajtee moo di mbiri xelaat. Su ma laajtee, "Lan la 
Aadama di xelaat?" dama bëgga ngeen wax ma mbir yi ngeen foog ne la Aadama doon 
xelaat. Accaleen ñu tontu laaj bi. Léegi, nanu tontu yeneen laaji "Lan" yi.  
· Read the question: What did Adama's father do to carry her so she would eat? Lan la 
baayi Aadama def ngir gàcca ko ndax mu lekka?
· Call on pupils at random to respond. (Baayi Aadama dafa gàcca Aadama)
· Read the question: Lan la yaayi Aadama fatte? Tontu: (Yaayi Aadama dafa fàtte ne 
joxoon na Aadama lekka)
· Call on pupils at random to respond.

the letter sound

board.

• Walk around, and listen to 5 pupils tell you the sound. If they don't all say the correct 
sound, tell pupils the sound, and then repeat. Do this up to 2 times.
Special assessment - Assess Week 3 vowels: tell the difference between short and long 
vowels
• Tell pupils you will say words with short and long vowels. Ask pupils to raise their hands. 
Pupils should put up 1 finger if it is a short vowel, and put up 2 fingers if it is a long vowel. 
Demonstrate for the first 2 words. Give pupils feedback to help them hear the vowels 
better (say the vowel sound with more emphasis to help them hear it).

Ask them what they know about it, or their experiences. (for example, "Have you seen 
this/it before?" "Where?" "What is it like?"). Discuss each picture on the pages for 1

picture. Ask pupils to do the same thing.

check what picture and letters they are touching.
• Continue to clap the words under each picture with them. After each word, ask them to 
find the matching vowels independently. Check their work as they go.
• Continue until both pages in the Pupil Book are done

activities.title: Vowel review
activities.content:
• Say: "Léegi damaa wax ab riir. Su ngeen ko déggee, ngeen teg seen baaraam ci ron

beneen baaraam te joxoñ ko ci araf bu mag bi."

 a  o  e  i

Review small and capital letters
• Review small and capital letters
e, A, i, o, E, a, I, O

activities.title: Teach the sound
activities.content:
Tongue twister-say the sound
• Say the tongue twister. Pupils repeat.
Laala log lii ci lexam Liisa laaj laala lu mu log ci lexam   
• Ask pupils what sound they hear most. Answer: /l/
Listening game - first sound 
• Say each word below. Pupils put a hand up if they hear the sound at the beginning of the  
 word and on the desk if they do not. 

Leb, Fés, Licin, laal, kaay, mu ne

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "l" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Bi moo di sunu arafu bés bi. Riiru araf bii moo di /l/. Accaleen nu waxandoor / l/".

• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).  
• Point to the capital letter "l" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Bii benna araf bi la. Moom itam riiru /l/. Su dee tàmbali baat walla tur, nii lanu koo   
 gise."
• Point to the small letter "l" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Li ci gën a bari, nii lanu koo gise ci baat yi"
Keyword picture study 
• Say: Lan ngeen gis?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say the   
 sound. 
• Say: Nanu ko waxandoor: /Lal/. Ndax dégga ngeen riiru /l/ ci baatu  /lal/?"
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.
Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: Baat bu fés bi moo di "lal".
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable is part  
 of the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is part of   
 the syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
· Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
· Point to the first syllable. Cover the "a" and show the "l"
· Say:  Lii ban riir la? pupils respond "l". (pupils respond "l") 
· Cover the "l" and show the "a."
· Say: Lii ban riir la?  (pupils respond "a")  
· Say: Mën ngeen a Jànga riir yi benna benna. Léegi ngeen boole leen ngir tabax dogiti 
baat. Léegi Jàngaleen riir yi te bu leen tàqale. /l//, /a/, "la"
· Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say 
each sound, and then the syllable. 

· After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the 
syllables independently again from their books.
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
· Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
· Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
· Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each 
column.
· Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to  
 it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
· Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
· Say: xoolleen fii te déglu Dinaa jànga dogiti baat yi te boole leen ngir tabax baat."  
· Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together  
 to read the word.
· Say: Accaleen nu jéemandoor.
· Read  the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils   
 to try reading the same word by themselves. 
· Say: Léegi nag xam ngeen lu ngeen war a def. Dañoo jànga yeneen baat ci seen téere yi   
 ni nu ko defewoon. Njékka leen na jànga dogiti baat yi, ngeen wax baat bi. Tegleen   
  seen baaraam te dawal.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of new and previously learned letters to read a short text independently.
Make predictions using a picture.
Write a new letter.

activities.title: My language
activities.content:
Teach a rule of the language 
·      Help pupils to find my language picture box in                  
the Pupil's Book.
• Say: When we're speaking or listen to words or sentences in our language, there are 
certain rules or guidelines that we must follow. These rules or guidelines helps others to 
understand clearly whatever we or others say to us. Today, let us listen to a new one.
• Am na ay yoon yu nu war a toppa sunu dee wax walla déglu ay baat ak ay kàddu yu nu war 
a toppa. Yoon yi dina nu jàppale ngir nu xam lu noo wax ci nun. Tey nanu déglu kàddu bu 
bees.
• Say: What do you see in the picture? Lan ngeen gis ci nataal bi?
·  Say: I am going to say a word or read a sentence. Listen attentively. Déglu leen bu baax,  
 damaa jànga kàddu.
Suma bët
Suma noppa.
Suma tanka  
• Say: Lan nga xam ci kàddu gi? ? Lan la tekki? (Answer: Ñaari kàddu yi moomeef la noo 
wone. Kàddu gu njékka gi di wone ne keneen na ko moom ñaarel bi di wone ne man maa ko 
moom). Lan ngeen xam ci kàddu gi? Lan la firi?
• Say: Which of the sentence or words shows what we see in the picture? Ban ci kàddu yii 
moo di firndél li ci natal bi?

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit   
 with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils  

 starting with the next pupil on the list.
• Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general  
 sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may   
 indicate that the child is struggling. 
• Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A    
 total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider   
 reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE 
Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils found 
challenging in the assessment. The skill reinforced by the 
activity is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or "syllable 
blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word? 
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to 
say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that 
starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next 
letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
•  Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have 
already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to 
participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
•  Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try  
to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and 
say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the   
sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who   
flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most 
of  the class has raised their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they 

are correct, give a clap of appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more 
syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
•  Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items   
 aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or   
 other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of    
 the syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they  
 get a clap of appreciation from the class

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the   
 pupil book. Read the first word.
• Say: Baat bii lan la tekki?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the   
 picture on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in   
 the list and whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for  
 the class. Ask all pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: Maa ngee xelaat ab baat. Baat bi moo di "Laalo". Accaleen nu tàccu "Laa/lo".
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil   
 Books. Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on  
 the board.
• Say: (Pupils read the word) Baat bi moo di "Laalo". Léegi binda nanu baat yi be noppi.   
 Accaleen nu jàngandoor.
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the   
 syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in  
 their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with  
 the rest of the words. 
• Words: laalo: laa/lo, lalal: la/lal,  words that can be made by syllables in the Pupil   
 Book
• Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Léegi, jéemleen ndax di ngeen mën a tabax seen baati boppa?
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they   
 know and write it in their copy books.
• When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a partner to share the word they made.

     Faatu Ak Weer Wi 

Faatu xale bu jigéen bu bég la, saayu nekka dafa dee fo ak moromam yi, rab yi, xob yi, doj yi 
ak léppa lu mu gis ci àlla bi.
Léeg léeg mu bëgga fo ak weer wi waay mënula jot weer wi mënu  koo laal.
Mu éeg ci garab gu gudda, mu foog ne di na jot waay betey jotu ko. Mu jél leket def  ci ndox 
be mu fees yóbbu ko fu sóri ngir mën faa gis takandeeru weer wi.. Mu dem ci néegam, gisatul 
weer wi. Mu xool ci seetu bi gis fa beneen weer waay moom xam na ne benna weer moo am. Bi 
weer wi feeñaatee mu betta ko mu waaru, mu dem ci lalam bi di jooy be baayam dégga ko.
Baayan ñow ci néegam ne ko: suma xarit bi, lan moo  xew? Lan nga nekka di jooy?
Faatu ne ko: man mënu maa jot weer wi! Baayam ne ko: Faatu doo musa mën a jot weer wi, li 
nga mën a jot moo di takandeeru weer wi. Faatu dafa foogoon ne, weer wi dafa
am takkandeer yu bari yoo xam ne xale yi di nañu ci mën a fo, waay weer wi nekka ci kow te 
kenna mënu  koo jot moom benna la. Faatu ne: Baax na, kon lóolu moo di  weer wi ci kow ñépp 
a ko bokka.

     Faatu Ak Weer Wi 

Faatu xale bu jigéen bu bég la, saa yu nekka dafa dee fo ak moromam yi, rab yi, xob yi, doj yi 
ak léppa lu mu gis ci àlla bi. 
Léegléeg mu bëgga fo ak weer wi waay mënula jot weer wi mënu koo laal. 
Mu éeg ci garab gu gudda, mu foog ne di na ko jot waay betey jotul ko. Mu jél leket def ci 
ndox Be mu fees yóbbu ko fu sóri ngir mën faa gis takandeeru weer wi. Mu dem ci néegam, 
gisatul weer wi. Mu xool ci seetu bi gis fa beneen weer waay moom xam na ne benna weer 
moo am. Bi weer wi feeñaatee mu betta ko mu waaru, mu dem ci lalam bi di jooy be baayam 
dégga ko. Baayam ñow ci néegam ne ko: suma xarit bi, lan moo xew? Lan ngaa jooy? 
Faatu ne ko: man mënu maa jot weer wi! Baayam ne ko: Faatu doo musa mën a jot weer 
wi, li nga mën a jot moo di takandeeru weer wi. Faatu dafa foogoon ne, weer wi dafa am 
takkandeer yu bari yoo xam ne xale yi dinanu ci mëna fo, waay weer wi nekka ci kow te kenna 
mënu koo jot moom benna la. Faatu ne: Baax na, kon lóolu moo di weer wi ci kow ñépp a ko 
bokka.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit   
 with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils  
 starting with the next pupil on the list. 

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general  
 sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may   
 indicate that the child is struggling.  
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A    
 total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider   
 reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40. 
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list.
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of  
 the  list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE 
Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils found 
challenging in the assessment. The skill reinforced by the 
activity is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or "syllable 
blending"
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to   
 say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that   
 starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next  
 letter. 

Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound  
 that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly  
 tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have   
 already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to   
 participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly.  

Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards   
 (try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant   

 and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the  
 sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who   
 flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until   
 most of the class has raised their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable.   
 If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10   
 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs.  
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items   
 aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other   
 place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables   
 they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of   
 appreciation from the class.

     Liiru Jaan
Benna bés, liiru jaan dafa jóge ci ab leket. Mu xool ci biti gis fa benna picca .Picca ma ne ko: 
"danga yéeme, lan moo tax nga mel nii? Lan moo tax amuloo mbagga?
Liiru jaan am naqar dem yoonam. Mu dajee ak njugub. Njugub ne ko: Liiru jaan danga 
yéeme, Lan moo tax nga mel nii?" Lan moo tax mënuloo naaw?" Liiru jaan faalewul ko, mu 
dem yoonam dajee ak mbotta. Mbotta ne ko: "Yéeme nga de? Lan moo tax nga mel nii? Yow 
amuloo tànka? Lan moo tax mënuloo tób "? Liiru jaan tàmbali jooy. Kon ndeke dama yéeme. 
Liiru jaan di jooy dem daje ak xargéeji. Xargéeji ne ko: "yow yaay lan? Liiru jaan tontu ko: 
Man xamuma sax man maa di kan ci naqar. Xargéeji ne ko , "demal seen kër seeti sa yaay." 
Liiru jaan dem gis fa yaayam, benna jaan ju réy bu ñuul di melax, amul mbagga, munul naaw, 
amul tanka, munul tób. Yaayam ne ko "suma doom; fan nga nekkon "? Liiru jaan muuñ. ci la 
xam ne moom nekkul kéemaan waay moom doomi jaan la mootax mu mel nii te nii la bindoo te 
doon liiru jaan rek doy na ko.

pupils.

·  Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.

should choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
· You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
· Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
· Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).

·  Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
·  Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
·  Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
·  Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
·  Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
·  Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of 
the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending". 
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
· Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to 
say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that 
starts with the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next 
letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
· Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have 
already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to 
participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
· Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant 
and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say 
the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who 
flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most 
of the class has raised their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they 
are correct, give a clap of appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more 
syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
· Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items 

aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other 
place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables 
they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of 
appreciation from the class.

their Pupil Books.

should choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
· You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit 
with you.
· Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 

· Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
· Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
· Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10).Next week you will assess 10 more 
pupils starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
· Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a 
general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 
may indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
· Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
· Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
· Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning 
of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
· Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to 
say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that 
starts with the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next 
letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
· Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have 
already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to 
participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
· Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant 
and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say 
the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who 
flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most 
of the class has raised their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they 
are correct, give a clap of appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more 
syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo

· Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items 
aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other 
place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables 
they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of 
appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:

pupil book. Read the first word.
· Say: What does this word mean?  Baat bi lan la tekki?
· Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the 
picture on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the 
list and whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the 
class. Ask all pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
· Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

baat yi. / da/ /ba/.
· Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil 
Books. Then, write the syllable on the board.
· Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on 
the board.
· Say: The word is "  ". Now we have written the whole word. Let us read together. Baat bi 
moo di " laka ". Léegi nanu binda baat bi yép. Accaleen nu jàngandoor.
· Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in 
their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with 
the rest of the words.
Words: Baba, Bale, kaba
Use syllables to build new words

· Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they 
know and write it in their copy books.

the word they made.

koo gise.

·    Say: Ban riiru araf la? (pupils respond "a").
·    Say:  Jàngaleen riir yi benna benna te nu tabax ci ay dogiti baat. Accaleen nu jàngandoor  
 riir yi te bu nu leen boole. /k./ /a./, 'ka'

·    Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say   
 each sound, and then the syllable. 
·    After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading

Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
·    Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.

baaraam te dawale.

the syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

pupils.

Pupil Books.

should choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
· You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit 
with you.

· Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
· Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
· Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
· Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
· Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may 
indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
· Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
· Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
· Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning 
of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE 
Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Based your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
· Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupil has learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts 
with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
· Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap 
the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate 
as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
· Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say 
its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). 
Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the flashcards. When 
they agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has 
raised their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a 
clap of appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to 
say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
· Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. 
Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hears all 3 of the syllables they wrote 
down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation 

from the class.

try the same word by themselves.

First, read the syllable and then say the word. Point with your finger and follow along.

    Baykat Bi Ak Mbaam iI 
Dafa amoom benna baykat bu dékka Baara. Bés bu nekka suba teel dafa dee dem ci toolam. 
Su àggee dafa dee liggéey bu baax, dina dog gajji yi yépp, ruuj tool bi be mu set, be noppi 
jëmbat fa ñambi. Ñambi bi jebbi te naat. Mu di ko bay be mu ñor, saa yu jóge si tool bi di na 
indi ñambi si kér gi. Baykat bi ku tabe la, mu mey ñépp mu sédda buur bi ak lingeer bi tamit.
Benna bés buur bi ne " nanu tànna benna bés ngir xew, ku nekka na indi li mu ñorle." Baykat 
bi ne ko "baax na Dinaa indi ñambi." Bi moo dem ci toolam bi mu daje ak mbaam. Mbaam nuyu 
ko ne ko "jàmma nga fanaan"! "Baykat bi fey ko ne ko: "jàmma rek." Mbaam ne ko "ndax 
mën nga maa dimbale ci kéwél mu ngee lekka suma tool bi rek." Baykat bi ne ko "su fekkee ne 
dinga ma dimbale, Dinaa la dimbale," mbaam nangu. Baykat bi war mbaam nu daxa kéwél. 
Kéwél di daw di cirib ciribi ci tool bi be récca. Kéwél la gën a gaaw mbaam waay baykat bi ne 
ko "am naa beneen pexe" mu uti ndénda. Mu tégga ndénda kéwél ñemewut téggi ndénda mu 
daw ndax raggal ndénda be tey dellusiwul. Bés bóobu betey kéwél ñowatul di lekka ci tooli 
mbaam mi.
Mbaam ne baykat bi "Dinaa la dimbale ebal la ñambi yi yóbbu ko ci kér buur". Ña nekkoon 
ci kër buur ñép bég, buur ne mbaam "ñun ñép a bég nanu si yow de, dañu bëgga nga dékka 
ak ñun su la neexee", ñu ñaan ko, mbaam nangu. Bés bóobu betey mbaam dékka kër buur di 
dimbale nit ñi.

· Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
